# Captions and table notes (figtab-repo -> paper-repo); one entry per delivered item

## Table 1 (appendix; tables/table1_audit.tex), generated by figs/table1_audit.py from experiment-repo results/audit.csv
Title: Data audit of the 13 binary score matrices after de-duplication.
Note: Rows are the file names of the data repository (commit 55faff49). Models: rows kept after dropping repeated model names and rows identical to an earlier row ("Dup. dropped" counts both). Families: distinct model families derived from the names by keyword (heuristic); for LegalBench the row-to-model mapping is not published, so families are unknown and every row counts as its own. Constant items: items answered identically by all models (kept). Full score: min / median / max of the models' full-benchmark accuracy. All matrices were checked to be binary.

## Fig. 1 (main text; figures/fig1_protocol.pdf), figs/fig1_protocol.py (no data)
Caption: The protocol. A design picks n items using only the source models' results; the target model is run on those n items only; an estimator turns its n answers (and the source matrix) into a predicted full-benchmark score, which is compared with the true score. The three splits differ in which models play the target.

## Table 2 (main text; tables/table2_primary.tex), figs/tables234.py from results/primary.csv
Title: Primary endpoint: RMSE of the predicted full score relative to uniform random sampling, n = 100 items.
Note: Entry = geometric mean over benchmarks of RMSE / RMSE of uniform × mean on the same targets and draws, [95% family-bootstrap interval; 2000 replicates, target families resampled within each benchmark]. Below 1 is better than uniform. Thin cells (< 10 targets or < 5 families) are excluded; the lineage split is defined for 12 benchmarks (LegalBench has no family information). Methods are design × estimator; the first seven rows are fixed class representatives (one per method class), the last three are the best methods by this endpoint and were chosen after seeing the results, so their intervals and ratios are optimistic. Second block: same quantity against stratified × mean as the baseline. The bottom rows count benchmarks, targets and target families, summed over the benchmarks entering. Benchmarks are not independent (HELM models recur across its benchmarks, OLL families across OLL benchmarks); the interval reflects target-family sampling only.
Appendix companions: table2_primary_all.tex (every method, non-thin benchmarks; longtable) and table2_primary_allbench.tex (every method, all benchmarks including thin cells; longtable).

## Fig. 2 (main text; figures/fig2_ratio_vs_n.pdf), figs/fig2_ratio_vs_n.py from results/ratio_by_n.csv.gz
Caption: RMSE of the predicted full score relative to uniform sampling (below 1 is better) against the number of items n, one panel per target split; log-log axes. Lines: geometric mean over non-thin benchmarks (13, 12 for lineage); bands: 95% family-bootstrap interval; one representative per method class plus the three best methods by the primary endpoint (chosen after the results, "post hoc"). In interpolation and lineage all source-aided methods start near half of uniform's RMSE at n = 10 and the ratio rises with n; the IRT-model and anchor plug-in predictors cross 1 at n ≈ 100–400, the difference-corrected methods stay near 0.7–0.8. In extrapolation the IRT-model and anchor plug-in predictors are above 1 from n = 25 and reach 3.8 at n = 400, while the difference-corrected and balanced methods stay at 0.7–0.9.

```console
\section{Experimental setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Data.}
We use the 13 binary item-by-model score matrices released with~\citep{zhang2025miss} (MIT licence; fixed commit given in the appendix): seven from the Open LLM Leaderboard v2 (ARC-Challenge, BBH, GPQA, IFEval, MMLU-Pro, MuSR, MATH Lvl~5) and six from HELM (CommonSense, GSM, LegalBench, MATH, MedQA, MMLU).
After dropping repeated model names and rows identical to an earlier row, a benchmark has between $79$ and $427$ models and between $437$ and $12{,}032$ items (Table~\ref{tab:audit}, appendix).
HELM's six benchmarks share models, and the leaderboard's families recur across its benchmarks, so the 13 benchmarks are not 13 independent replications.

\paragraph{Protocol.}
For every benchmark and each of the three splits of Section~\ref{sec:method}, every method receives only the source matrix, selects $n$ items, and sees the target's answers on them; its estimate is scored against the target's true full score.
All methods use the same $n$ and the same subset draws, ten per fold and $n$ (forty for extrapolation), and one subset serves all targets of a draw.
The grid is $n\in\{10,25,50,100,200,400\}$ restricted to $n\le N/2$.
The primary endpoint, fixed before any target was scored, is the RMSE of a method divided by the RMSE of uniform sampling with the sample mean at $n=100$ on the same targets and draws, aggregated over benchmarks by the geometric mean.
Its 95\% interval is a bootstrap over target families (families resampled within each benchmark, ratio formed within each replicate).
A (benchmark, split) with fewer than $10$ targets or fewer than $5$ independent families among the targets is called thin; thin cells are left out of the primary aggregate, which is also reported with them.
As $n=100$ is $18\%$ of the items of IFEval and under $1\%$ of those of MMLU-Pro, a second endpoint fixes $n/N=2\%$.
Ordering is scored by Spearman and Kendall correlations per fold and draw over that fold's targets and then averaged, by top-decile precision, and by pairwise accuracy as a function of the true gap.

\paragraph{Methods compared.}
We compare 7 designs and the estimator groups of Section~\ref{sec:method}: calibrated regression, IRT, kNN and ridge predictors, each as a model estimator, a plug-in estimator and a difference estimator.
The anchor-point, tinyBenchmarks-style (anchor design with IRT plug-in) and metabench-style (information-top design with calibrated-regression or IRT model estimators) methods are our re-implementations of their selection and prediction steps; they are not the published code and differ in the IRT fitter, the item embedding and the regression step.
We did not run the assessor~\citep{pacchiardi2024100}, the active evaluation acquisition~\citep{li2025active}, SubLIME~\citep{saranathan-etal-2025-sublime}, nor the released implementations of the comparison study.
About one hundred (design, estimator) combinations were run; where the text names the best of them it is the best of this pre-registered grid chosen after the outcomes, and we state claims about method classes.
```

cd /hutian/repo; cat > /tmp/req.md <<'E'
`paper-repo` `dev` now has the results text (`paper/sections/results.tex`, methods in `method.tex`, setup in `setup.tex`), written from results-v1 and figtab's delivered Table 2 and Figs. 2–6. Please confirm, from the code that computes each, what the text says each number *is* (not only its value), and correct what is wrong. Reply once, with the changes.

1. **Method section** (`method.tex`, "Designs", "Predictors and estimators"): the PPS formula and floor, stratified (one random item per block of N/n difficulty-ordered items), balanced (greedy from a pool of 4n against all sources' full scores), anchor (k-means k=n, medoid weighted by cluster size), info-top/CAT (2PL Fisher information), calreg/irt(d=2)/knn/ridge, the Hájek mean, plug-in, difference estimator with 5-fold cross-fitted residuals over the sample, and the hyperparameter grids (ε, k, α, λ) and inner splits. Is the cross-fitting over the *sample* (as written) and are ε and λ chosen per (benchmark, fold, n)?
2. **Setup** (`setup.tex`): 10 subset draws per fold and n, 40 for extrapolation; n grid; thin-cell rule; "about one hundred (design, estimator) combinations" (104 methods in `primary.csv`).
3. **Table 2 rows 1–7**: the text calls them "one fixed representative per method class". How were they chosen (before or after the outcomes)? If after, I will say so.
4. **Fig. 5 numbers** used in the text: observed geometric mean 0.70 vs predicted 0.81 (interpolation/lineage, left panel, source item means) and 0.85 vs 0.85 (extrapolation); which of the two panels and which split(s) do these belong to? And is the text's definition of q (fraction of the Bernoulli variance of the unsampled items explained, 1 − Brier(predictor)/Brier(constant)) right?
5. **Fixed-λ rows** (`fixed:diff-irt@1.0`): text says "λ=1 with the other hyperparameters fixed" — what exactly is fixed (ε, k)? In extrapolation tuned and fixed give 0.85/0.85 (uniform), 0.82/0.78 (balanced), 0.85/0.82 (PPS), so the outline's "tuned λ is too shrunk in extrapolation" is not visible in these numbers beyond the balanced/PPS designs. Is there a larger-gap nested split (top 25–50 % of sources)?
6. **Waiting for**: the target-recalibrated estimator and two-phase design (Brief rev 3–4), n/N = 2 % endpoint, M-source runs, LOBO-selected rows, bias² column. The text for extrapolation will be rewritten when they arrive; tell me when and under which file names.
E
